title: Metered bands playbook
content:
Purpose:
- Quick, portable scratchpad for metered / per-token band ideas. Not final, meant to capture assumptions and first-pass math for pricing experiments and early PLG thresholds.

Assumptions (pick one set as baseline for growth deck):
- Model mix (blended): 40% small opt-style (cheap), 40% medium 2-8B, 20% large 70B+ quant.
- Cost to Redwood (inference only, amortized infra + mgmt + network):
  * small: $0.02 per 1k tokens
  * medium: $0.10 per 1k tokens
  * large: $0.40 per 1k tokens
- Blended cost calc: 0.4*0.02 + 0.4*0.10 + 0.2*0.40 = 0.008 + 0.04 + 0.08 = $0.128 per 1k tokens (~$0.13).
- Target gross margin: 60% (initial), sustainable target 50% at scale if we subsidize growth.

Retail price (baseline math):
- Price = cost / (1 - margin). For 60% margin => price = 0.128 / 0.4 = $0.32 per 1k tokens.
- Check: For 10M tokens -> revenue = (10,000 * $0.32) = $3,200; cost = (10,000 * $0.128) = $1,280; gross = $1,920 (60%).

Quick sensitivity table (blended cost | retail @60% | retail @50%):
- $0.08 | $0.20 | $0.16
- $0.13 | $0.32 | $0.26
- $0.25 | $0.63 | $0.50

Band proposals (metered per-1k pricing; examples to A/B test):
- Free / hobby: 0 - 50k tokens/mo free (credit). Encourage exploration.
- Developer: 50k - 2M tokens/mo -> $0.40 per 1k (introduces simple, slightly-premium pricing for on-demand developers).
- Growth: 2M - 50M tokens/mo -> $0.30 per 1k (baseline retail from blended cost above).
- Scale: 50M - 500M tokens/mo -> $0.19 per 1k (volume discount; still ~45% margin on baseline blended cost).
- Enterprise / Reserved: >500M or committed -> custom pricing, e.g., $0.08 - $0.14 per 1k depending on commitment and model mix, plus Dedicated reservation upsell.

Alternative: per-request buckets for chat-heavy apps (message-level). Example: bill by input+output tokens but normalize to 1k-unit with floor of 8 tokens for tiny calls.

Committed / Dedicated combos:
- Offer committed capacity discount (reserve X GPUs or Y tokens/mo). If customer commits to a monthly burn, offer 20-50% off metered price depending on length and rigidity of commit.
- Tie reserved discounts to SLA tier and on-prem/private add-ons.

Billing nuances / product decisions to capture now:
- Metering granularity: bill per 1k tokens with 1-token precision on usage side, but round final invoice to nearest 100 tokens to keep bill size reasonable.
- Minimum invoice: $5/mo for active accounts to reduce churn noise.
- Free credits: 1,000,000 tokens for new signups (one-time) or first 30 days? Recommendation: 30-day free $ credits, not permanent token allowance.
- Overages: if a customer hits a committed bucket, auto-bill at next tier unless customer has explicit cap.

Unit-econ examples (toy customers):
- Tiny app: 200k tokens/mo, uses developer band at $0.40/1k => revenue = 200 * 0.40 = $80/mo. Cost = 200 * 0.128 = $25.6 -> gross = $54.4 (68%).
- Mid app: 8M tokens/mo, growth band at $0.30/1k => rev = 8000 * 0.30 = $2,400. Cost = 8000 * 0.128 = $1,024 -> gross = $1,376 (57%).
- Large app: 120M tokens/mo, scale pricing at $0.19/1k => rev = 120000 * 0.19 = $22,800. Cost = 120000 * 0.128 = $15,360 -> gross = $7,440 (33%) => suggests need for deeper discounts only if we can move them to Dedicated/Reserved where infra cost per token drops.

Key levers to improve unit economics (notes to ourselves):
- Push high-volume customers to Dedicated or Private where effective cost per token drops via reserved infra and locality.
- Quantization + model selection guidance: recommend smaller models for prompt fragments, rerank with embeddings only when necessary.
- Introduce automatic caching / prefix caching as product features and charge for cache warming separately? (or include in higher tiers).
- Batching and concurrency defaults: give SDK/options to lower cost with minimal dev changes.

Open questions / experiments to run:
- How sensitive is sign-up conversion to per-1k price vs. free-credit size? A/B: $0.40/1k + 1M credit vs $0.30/1k + 200k credit.
- Test the developer band floor: is $0.40/1k too high for hobbyists? Consider $0.20/1k but gate usage with rate limits.
- Do customers prefer a single blended price or model-tiered prices (e.g., cheaper for opt-small, expensive for L70B)? Simpler is blended but less precise.
- How to show cost transparency in billing: line items per-model or only aggregated? (customers ask for per-model breakdown).

Operational notes:
- Ensure analytics surface: tokens by model, peak QPS, average tokens per request, percent of requests hitting cached prefixes. Those directly map to our cost model and margin monitoring.
- Add billing hooks to console: forecast X-month burn if current growth continues + recommended reserved package.

Next steps (immediate):
1) Wire up a small experiment in sandbox accounts to charge at Developer vs Growth band for new signups (A/B). Owner: Priya. (JIRA-PRIC-88).
2) Build a simple unit-econ dashboard for product team with selectable blended assumptions (weights by model). Owner: Liam.
3) Draft a short one-pager for Sales that explains when to push Dedicated vs. metered; include migration path and margin math. Owner: Marta.

Notes to future self:
- Keep this doc lightweight; copy relevant bits into Confluence when we converge.
- Remember margin targets shift if we include support, data retention, and eval costs in the backed-in "cost" metric. Right now numbers are inference-only and optimistic.

Random heuristics I found useful:
- Ballpark: $0.25-$0.35 / 1k is a comfortable "retail" zone for mid-2024 models at 60% margin if blended cost ~ $0.10-$0.15/1k.
- Big corp customers expect ~30-50% discount at scale or will ask for Dedicated.

End of quick scratchpad.
